questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to acquire citizenship in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Renunciation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Renunciation** is not a way to acquire citizenship in India; rather, it is a way to voluntarily give up Indian citizenship.
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, provides various modes for acquiring Indian citizenship, including **by birth, descent, registration, and naturalization**.
 
• **Incorporation of territory** is another mode where a new territory becomes a part of India, and the government may specify the persons who shall be citizens of India.
 
• Citizenship by **registration** is available to certain categories of persons such as persons of Indian origin who are ordinarily resident in India and other specified categories.
 
• Citizenship by **birth** is applicable to individuals born in India on or after January 26, 1950, but before July 1, 1987, and to individuals born on or after July 1, 1987, if either parent is a citizen of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, also provides for the termination and deprivation of citizenship under specific conditions.
 
• Renunciation of citizenship is a voluntary act and can be done by any citizen of India who is also a citizen or national of another country.
 
• Upon renunciation, the individual ceases to be a citizen of India, and any minor child of that person also loses Indian citizenship.
 
• The process of renunciation is outlined in the Citizenship Rules, and it requires the individual to make a declaration in the prescribed manner.
 
• It's important for individuals to be aware of the implications of renunciation, including the loss of rights and privileges associated with Indian citizenship.

questions.question: In which part of the Indian constitution are the provisions related to panchayat mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Panchayati Raj

 
 
• Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government of villages in rural India as opposed to urban and suburban municipalities.
 
• It consists of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through which the self-government of villages is realized.
 
• They are tasked with "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• ​Part IX of the Indian Constitution is the section of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats.
 
• It stipulates that in states or Union Territories with more than two million inhabitants there are three levels of PRIs:
 
 
• Zilla Parishad at the District Level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the Block Level
 
• Gram/Village Panchayat at the Village Level
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act,1992 added Article 243 to Article 243O and a new part Part IX to the constitution of India.
 
• Salient features of this Act:
 
 
• Gram Sabha (Article 243A):
 
 
• ​A body of all persons registered in the electoral roll of that Panchayat.
 
 
 
• Three-Tier System (Article 243B):
 
 
• ​Panchayat at the village, intermediate, and district levels.
 
 
 
• The election of members and chairpersons are given under Article 243B.
 
• Reservation of seats for SC/ST is provided at all three levels under Article 243D.
 
• The duration of Panchayats is given under Article 243E, it is constituted for five years.
 
• Grounds of disqualification are given under Article 243F.
 
• Powers, authorities, and responsibilities are given in Article 243G and enlisted in the 11th schedule of the constitution.
 
• State Election Commission (243K) for superintendence, control, and direction of the election in Panchayats.

questions.question: The Parliament of India has passed the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002, which establishes the basic rights of primary education for children between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 - 14 Years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by the Parliament of India in December 2002, and it came into effect on July 1, 2003.
 
• This amendment inserted Article 21A in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It made it mandatory for the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children in this age group.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, was enacted to operationalize this constitutional mandate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendment:**

 
 
• A constitutional amendment is a change made to the Constitution of a country, which requires a specific procedure to be followed for its adoption.
 
• In India, a constitutional amendment requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in certain cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A:**
 
 
• Article 21A was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• It stipulates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years in a manner determined by law.
 
 
 
• **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009:**
 
 
• The RTE Act was enacted to give effect to Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It mandates that every child has a right to full-time elementary education of satisfactory and equitable quality in a formal school which satisfies certain essential norms and standards.
 
• It also lays down the responsibilities of the State, parents, schools, and teachers to ensure the implementation of this right.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Amendment:**
 
 
• This amendment has significantly increased the enrollment rates in primary schools across India.
 
• It has also brought attention to issues such as infrastructure, quality of education, and teacher training in the Indian educational system.

questions.question: Judicial Review, a salient feature of the Constitution of India, has been borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The US**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicial Review** in India has been borrowed from the **United States** Constitution.
 
• It is a process under which executive or legislative actions are subject to review by the judiciary.
 
• This feature helps in ensuring the constitutionality of laws and acts as a check on the powers of the legislature and executive.
 
• The concept of Judicial Review in India is enshrined in **Article 13** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It plays a crucial role in protecting the fundamental rights of citizens and maintaining the supremacy of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• c
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: The Seventy-First Amendment to the Indian Constitution included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages in the _____ Schedule.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** 71st Amendment**, **enacted in 1992,** added **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages** to the** Eighth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution, recognizing them as **official languages of India.**
 
• The amendment was a significant step towards** linguistic inclusivity, acknowledging the cultural and linguistic diversity **of India and granting official status to these languages.
 
• The 71st Amendment highlighted the importance of **preserving and promoting** these languages, ensuring their** protection**, and **facilitating educational resources, official documentation, and communication** in these languages for their respective communities.
 
• The addition of **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali** languages to the Eighth Schedule aimed to provide representation and support to linguistic communities in **Goa, Manipur, and Sikkim, respectively.​**

questions.question: Any citizen of India can make a declaration renouncing his/her Indian citizenship under the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Citizenship Act, 1955**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** is the primary legislation governing the acquisition and loss of Indian citizenship.
 
• Under this Act, any Indian citizen can renounce their Indian citizenship by making a declaration.
 
• The renunciation of citizenship is a formal process detailed in the Act and ensures that the individual is no longer considered an Indian citizen.
 
• The Act also covers other aspects of citizenship such as acquisition, termination, and registration of citizenship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955**

 
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, provides the basis for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
 
• It specifies five modes of acquiring citizenship: by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• The Act outlines the processes and criteria for each mode, ensuring clear guidelines for obtaining Indian citizenship.
 
• Amendments to the Act have been made over the years to address various aspects of citizenship and to update the legal framework in line with changing needs and circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Renunciation of Citizenship**
 
 
• Renunciation of citizenship is a voluntary act where an individual formally declares their intention to give up Indian citizenship.
 
• This process is essential for individuals who wish to acquire citizenship of another country that does not allow dual citizenship.
 
• The declaration must be made in the prescribed manner, and upon its acceptance, the individual ceases to be an Indian citizen.
 
• Renunciation also extends to any minor children of the individual, but they have the right to resume Indian citizenship upon reaching adulthood.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI)**
 
 
• The OCI scheme provides a form of residency status to persons of Indian origin who are citizens of other countries, allowing them to live and work in India indefinitely.
 
• OCI cardholders do not have the right to vote, hold constitutional office, or buy agricultural land, but they enjoy many of the same rights as Indian citizens.
 
• This scheme facilitates easier travel to and from India and allows for long-term residency without the need for repeated visa applications.

questions.question: Which directive principle has been implemented in establishing Handloom and Handicrafts Boards?

options.text: Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis
Participation of workers in management of Industries
Provision for just and humane condition of work

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis** is a directive principle implemented in establishing Handloom and Handicrafts Boards.
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These are provided in Part IV of the Constitution of India.
 
• The aim of these principles is to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They act as a yardstick in the hands of the people to measure the performance of the government.
 
• Promotion of cottage industries on a cooperative basis helps in the economic development of rural areas and provides employment opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to promote social and economic democracy.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• However, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, and it is the duty of the state to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• Some other important directive principles include the provision for adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, protection of childhood and youth, and organization of village panchayats.

__
 
• **The preamble** mentions **"Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship"** as one of the noble ideals mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Indian Constitution's preamble outlines the** fundamental principles** and** values** that guide the country and its people.
 
• It begins with the words** "We, the people of India,"** emphasizing the democratic nature of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian Constitution** is the ultimate law of the land based on the idea put forth by **M.N. Roy.**

• The **Government of India Act 1935 **was superseded by the constitution in **1935**, transforming the Dominion of India into the **Republic of India.**

questions.question: Income of the state which arises out of the property left by the people without a legal heir is called ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Escheat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Income of the state which arises out of the property left by the people without a legal heir is termed **Escheat**.
 
• **Escheat** refers to the right of a government to require ownership of estate assets or unclaimed property.
 
• It most ordinarily occurs when an individual **dies** with no will and no heirs.
 
• Escheat rights may be granted when **assets** are unclaimed for a proctored period of your time.
 
• These situations may also be mentioned to as** bona vacantia** or just unclaimed property.
 
• The concept of escheat maintains that property always includes a **recognized owner**, which might be the state or government if no other claimants to ownership exist or are readily identified.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **writ** is a formal written order issued by a body with administrative or judicial jurisdiction; in modern usage, this body is usually a court. 
 
• “**from the new**” When a court hears a case **de novo**, it is deciding the problems without reference to any legal conclusion or assumption made by the previous court to listen to the case.
 
• A **felony** is traditionally considered a crime of high seriousness, whereas a misdemeanor is regarded as less serious.

questions.question: The government scheme, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana aims for crop insurance service for farmers. This type of government efforts falls under ________ of the Directive Principles of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Act added the Right to Education to the Indian constitution?

__
 
• Article 21 A was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002.

 
 
• This article declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such a manner as the State may determine.
 
• This article deals with the concept of inclusive education, Specific terms in inclusive education such as Impairment, Disability, Special Educational Needs, Learning Difficulties, Reasons For Inclusion, Provisions for Children With Special Needs, etc.

questions.question: By which amendment of the Indian Constitution the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**42nd Amendment Act, 1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The ‘Preamble’ of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• It is a brief introductory statement that sets out the guiding purpose and principles of the document, and it indicates the source from which the document which derives its authority, meaning, the people.
 
• It was adopted on 26 November 1949 by the Constituent Assembly of India and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• **After the 42nd amendment, three new terms "Socialist, Secular, and Integrity" were added to the Preamble. Hence, Option 2 is correct.**
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** is one of the most important amendments to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was enacted by the** Indian National Congress** headed by **Indira Gandhi** then.
 
• Due to the large number of amendments this act has brought to the Indian Constitution, it is also known as the** ‘Mini-Constitution.’ **
 
• Only one time the Preamble was amended in 1976 till date.
 
• Thus, we can say that the words "Socialist and Secular" were added to the Preamble through the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

questions.question: Provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection are mentioned under which schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**10th schedule.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__​**

__
 
• **10th schedule:-****​**

 
 
• It includes provisions relating to the disqualification of the members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of defection.
 
• This schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, also known as the Anti-defection Law. 
 
• The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution is designed to prevent the evil or mischief of political defections motivated by the lure of office or material benefits or other similar considerations.
 
• It is intended to strengthen the fabric of Indian parliamentary democracy by curbing unprincipled and unethical political defections.
 
 
 
• **Grounds for disqualification:-**
 
 
• If an elected member gives up his membership in a political party voluntarily.
 
• If he votes or abstains from voting in the House, contrary to any direction issued by his political party.
 
• If any member who is independently elected joins any party.
 
• If any nominated member joins any political party after the end of 6 months.
 
• The decision on disqualification questions on the ground of defection is referred to the Speaker or the Chairman of the House, and his/her decision is final.
 
• All proceedings in relation to disqualification under this Schedule are considered to be proceedings in Parliament or the Legislature of a state as is the case.
 
 
 
• **​Exceptions Under the Anti-Defection Law:-**
 
 
• In a situation **where two-thirds of the legislators of a political party decide to merge into another party, neither the members who decide to join nor the ones who stay with the original party will face disqualification. **
 
• Any **person elected as chairman or speaker can resign from his party, and rejoin the party if he demits that post. **
 
• Earlier, the law allowed parties to be split, but at present, this has been outlawed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Ninth Schedule

 
 
 
It deals with the state acts and regulations that deal with land reforms and

 
abolition of the zamindari system. It also deals with the acts and regulations of the Parliament dealing with other matters.

 
Note: 1st Amendment Act 1951 added the Ninth Schedule to protect the laws included in it from judicial scrutiny on the ground of violation of fundamental rights.

 
However, in 2007, the Supreme Court ruled that the laws included in this schedule after

 
April 24, 1973, are now open to judicial review

 
 
 

 
 
Eleventh Schedule

 
 
 
It contains the provisions that specify the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats. It has 29 matters.

 
Note: This schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992

 
 
 

 
 
Twelfth Schedule

 
 
 
It deals with the provisions that specify the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities. It has 18 matters.

 
Note: This schedule was added by the 74th Amendment Act of 1992

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution divides the power between the Centre and the state in terms of the union, state and concurrent list?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Seventh Schedule.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India defines and specifies allocation of powers and functions between Union & States
 
• It contains three lists; i.e. 1) Union List, 2) State List and 3) Concurrent List. 
 
• Originally there was 97 subjects in union list but now it is 100 subjects in union list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Ninth Schedule was brought in the Indian Constitution on 18 June 1951 to abolish the Zamindari system. 
 
• The third Schedule contains the “Forms of Oaths or Affirmations” of various constitutional posts. 
 
• The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas as well as of Scheduled Tribes residing in any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
